Stabilizer averaging proves the kernel is proportional to the monic hypergeometric orthogonal cubic, constant diagonal fixes it to d_3 h(J)/h(k), and transitivity, symmetry and idempotence give the common absolute-row-sum norm and E K²=d_3. The repaired sparse limit follows from the overlap factorial moments, positivity of the limiting Poisson Gram system, h(k)~k³ and uniform integrability via d_3/n³. The factorial generating identity verifies the Charlier cubic. At λ=3 the sole integer root j=1 yields exactly e^(−λ) λ^(3/2)|3−λ|/6 in Φ(√λ); all other terms have continuously differentiable sum, giving 6e^(−3) in the c variable. The four leading terms at λ↓0 and the standardized Poisson cubic at λ→∞ give the stated end behavior. At positive density the hypergeometric CLT and exponential tails give Gram convergence, and (k−μ)/σ=√(n−1) fixes the Gaussian kernel normalization. The original finite formula was also correct (Hahn flux identity and alternating signs including integer roots), but does not survive as a novelty claim. `python3 /workspace/reviews/evidence/reproduce.py 5` independently formed exact inclusion-matrix projections for (6,3),(7,3),(8,4),(9,4), checking norms 2, 16/5, 12/5 and 32/7 and the background finite identity. These checks are not the proof of the limit or cusp; the frozen verifier was inspected, not executed.
